lab.generationDescription: The lab generates random monthly values with no underlying trend to show how month-to-month persistence can produce false alarms.
lab.generationTooltipHtml:
How these data are generated
The lab generates random monthly values with no underlying trend to show how month-to-month persistence can produce false alarms.
lab.noiseTitle: Can noise look like a trend?
lab.noiseDescriptionHtml: This series has no underlying trend. Nearby months can have similar values, which can lead either test to flag a trend.
lab.frequencyDescription: Both tests use the same 200 series with zero trend. The third bar shows the 5% reference rate.
lab.honestTest: Expected false-alarm rate for a well-calibrated test at the 5% threshold.
lab.batchSummary: {runs} synthetic series · {years} years each · memory {memory}. Whiskers show 95% Wilson intervals.
lab.loadError: Could not load the simulation. Try again.
lab.spikeTitle: Can two spikes tilt a trend?
lab.spikeDescription: Two unusually high months near the end of this synthetic series pull the fitted line upward. Compare it with the fit to the original values.
lab.spikeLesson: The rest of the series stays the same. In real records, check whether extreme values are genuine and see how much they affect the fit.

methods.toolDescriptionHtml: Pick NASA Earth data and a place. See what changes, where, how fast, and whether it is significant – then check if it holds for other periods.
methods.references: References: Santer B.D. et al. (2000) J. Geophys. Res. 105, 7337–7356 · Hirsch R.M., Slack J.R., Smith R.A. (1982) Water Resour. Res. 18, 107–121 · Sen P.K. (1968) JASA 63, 1379–1389 · Benjamini Y., Hochberg Y. (1995) JRSS-B 57, 289–300 · Wilks D.S. (2016) BAMS 97, 2263–2273.
methods.limitsTitle: What the tool will not tell you
methods.limitsDescription: A trend is not a cause. The tool never says “the climate is not changing” or “humans caused this”: it reports what this series, place and period can and cannot show.

deseasonalisation.label: deseasonalisation
deseasonalisation.text: Each calendar month's mean over the selected period is subtracted (anomalies).

trend.label: trend
trend.text: Ordinary least squares slope of the anomalies, reported per decade.

uncertainty.label: uncertainty
uncertainty.text: 95% confidence interval with AR(1) effective sample size correction (Santer et al. 2000).

cross_check.label: cross check
cross_check.text: Seasonal Mann–Kendall test and seasonal Sen slope (Hirsch et al. 1982).

map_multiple_testing.label: map multiple testing
map_multiple_testing.text: Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate across map cells, q = 0.05 (Wilks 2016).

regional_mean.label: regional mean
regional_mean.text: cos(latitude)-weighted mean of cell anomalies; months with < 50% area coverage are dropped.

minimum_data.label: minimum data
minimum_data.text: A trend is computed only if at least {percent}% of the selected months are valid.

insufficient_data.title: Not enough data
insufficient_data.text: Too many gaps or too few years. Try a longer period or a bigger area.

ci_includes_zero.title: No clear trend
ci_includes_zero.text: The range of likely slopes includes zero. That is not proof of no change.

depends_on_period.title: Depends on the period
depends_on_period.text: Significant here, but many other start/end years disagree. Be careful.

trend_detected.title: Trend detected
trend_detected.agree: Significant at 5%, corrected for autocorrelation. Mann–Kendall agrees.
trend_detected.disagree: Significant at 5%, corrected for autocorrelation. Mann–Kendall does not confirm it – check outliers.

ndvi.name: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
ndvi.question: Greener or browner?
ndvi.definition: NDVI compares red and near-infrared light reflected by plants; higher values mean denser, healthier green vegetation (−0.2 water/bare … 0.9 dense forest).
ndvi.provider: NASA LP DAAC; COG mirror on Microsoft Planetary Computer
ndvi.resolution: 500 m product, averaged to 0.1° grid (≈ 8–11 km)
ndvi.license: NASA EOSDIS data: no restrictions on reuse (NASA Earth Science Data Policy)
ndvi.citation: Didan, K. (2021). MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 500m SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13A1.061
caveats: Monthly value = mean of 16-day composites starting in that month, read from 8× COG overviews (≈ 4 km) before averaging to 0.1°.
The per-pixel quality layer is not applied in this prototype; values outside the valid range are removed.
Terra's orbit drifted after 2022; the default period stops at 2024.
A change in NDVI can come from land-use change (clearing, irrigation), not only from climate.

lst_day.name: Daytime land surface temperature
lst_day.question: Hotter ground by day?
lst_day.definition: How hot the ground/canopy surface is around 10:30 local time, measured from space in clear-sky conditions – not the air temperature you feel.
lst_day.provider: NASA LP DAAC; COG mirror on Microsoft Planetary Computer
lst_day.resolution: 1 km product, averaged to 0.1° grid (≈ 8–11 km)
lst_day.license: NASA EOSDIS data: no restrictions on reuse (NASA Earth Science Data Policy)
lst_day.citation: Wan, Z., Hook, S., Hulley, G. (2021). MODIS/Terra Land Surface Temperature/Emissivity 8-Day L3 Global 1km SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD11A2.061
caveats: Only clear-sky observations exist: cloudy months contribute fewer values (see coverage).
Monthly value = mean of 8-day composites starting in that month, read from 4× COG overviews (≈ 4 km).
Terra's overpass time drifted after 2022; the default period stops at 2024.

lst_day_aqua.name: Afternoon land surface temperature (Aqua)
lst_day_aqua.question: Does a second satellite agree?
lst_day_aqua.definition: Same measurement as the Terra daytime surface temperature, but from the Aqua satellite passing around 13:30 local time; its orbit was kept stable until 2022, so it is a useful cross-check.
lst_day_aqua.provider: NASA LP DAAC; COG mirror on Microsoft Planetary Computer
lst_day_aqua.resolution: 1 km product, averaged to 0.1° grid (≈ 8–11 km)
lst_day_aqua.license: NASA EOSDIS data: no restrictions on reuse (NASA Earth Science Data Policy)
lst_day_aqua.citation: Wan, Z., Hook, S., Hulley, G. (2021). MODIS/Aqua Land Surface Temperature/Emissivity 8-Day L3 Global 1km SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MYD11A2.061
caveats: Aqua starts in mid-2002; the cube starts in 2003 (first complete year).
Afternoon surface temperature differs from morning (Terra) values; compare trends, not levels.
Aqua's orbit also began drifting after 2022.

t2m.name: Air temperature at 2 m
t2m.question: Warmer air?
t2m.definition: Monthly mean air temperature two metres above the ground, from the NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis (a model that assimilates observations).
t2m.provider: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project
t2m.license: NASA POWER data: free to use, acknowledgement requested
t2m.citation: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project, funded through the NASA Earth Science/Applied Science Program; MERRA-2 (Gelaro et al., 2017, J. Climate).
caveats: Reanalysis = model constrained by observations; not a direct satellite measurement.

precip.name: Precipitation
precip.question: More or less rain?
precip.definition: Average amount of rain and snow reaching the ground per day, from MERRA-2 corrected with observed precipitation.
precip.provider: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project
precip.license: NASA POWER data: free to use, acknowledgement requested
precip.citation: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project; MERRA-2 bias-corrected precipitation (Reichle et al., 2017).
caveats: Precipitation varies a lot year to year: long periods are needed before a trend is detectable.
Planned upgrade: GPM IMERG monthly (needs NASA Earthdata Login).

soil_root.name: Root-zone soil wetness
soil_root.question: Drier or wetter soil?
soil_root.definition: How full the soil water store is in the root zone (top ~1 m): 0 = completely dry, 1 = saturated. Modelled by MERRA-2.
soil_root.provider: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project
soil_root.license: NASA POWER data: free to use, acknowledgement requested
soil_root.citation: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project; MERRA-2 land surface (Reichle et al., 2017).
caveats: Model estimate: irrigation and groundwater pumping are not represented.
Planned independent check: SMAP (2015–) or GRACE water storage (needs Earthdata Login).

gistemp.name: Surface temperature anomaly (GISTEMP v4)
gistemp.question: Where is it warming fastest?
gistemp.definition: Difference between the monthly surface temperature and its 1951–1980 average, combining weather stations on land and ships/buoys at sea.
gistemp.product: GISTEMP v4, 1200 km smoothing, GHCNv4 + ERSSTv5
gistemp.provider: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies
gistemp.license: NASA GISS data: free to use with citation
gistemp.citation: GISTEMP Team (2026). GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA GISS. Lenssen et al. (2019, 2024).
caveats: Grid cells far from stations are filled from neighbours up to 1200 km away; polar and early-period values are less certain.
Small regions contain only a few 2° cells.
